ch.s: Verses 1–4: “At that time, after the death of Joshua, the children of the Canaanites were still in the land, and the Israelites resolved to drive them out.”; Verses 5–8: “And they fought with Adonibezek in Bezek, and he fled from before them, and they pursued him and caught him, and they took hold of him and cut…”; Verses 9–12: “And the children of Joseph spied out Bethel, and the watchmen saw a man going forth from the city, and they caught him and said to him, Show…”; Verses 13–16: “And all the elders also fought the battles of Israel against the Canaanites and the Lord drove the Canaanites from before the children of Israel, in order to…”; Verse 17: “Strengthen yourselves, and let the hearts of all you that trust in the Lord be of good courage.”. People named: Joshua, Simeon, Joseph, Luz, Abraham, Isaac. Places: Judah, Bezek, Bethel, Jerusalem, City.
q: Read verses 1–4. What is happening, and what stands out to you most?
In verses 5–8, what do you learn about war and conflict?
Read verse 13 slowly. What does it say about God, about people, and about how to live?
What does Joshua’s part in this chapter teach you — as an example to follow or a warning to heed?
Where do you see the theme of leadership and kingship in this chapter, and how does it connect to the rest of The Book of Jasher?
What is one specific way you can put this chapter into practice this week?
ch.a: Thank God for His deliverance, and share what He has done for you with one person.
